subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu long-reply streaming latency be handled by an explicit append/full-content mode, a different full-content coalescing strategy, or no behavior change until live proof identifies a safe contract?
rationale: The bug is real enough to keep open, but the remaining choice changes Feishu's user-visible streaming contract and may trade latency against prior truncation protection.

options.title: Require Live Proof Then Pick Mode
options.body: Collect redacted Feishu timing and CardKit PUT evidence, then reshape the fix around the mitigation that actually reduces the tail without losing final content.

options.title: Accept Coalescing As Default
options.body: Proceed with the linked coalescing direction if maintainers decide the smoother-contract tradeoff is acceptable despite the latest report that it may not be enough.

options.title: Keep Full-Content Only
options.body: Reject append-mode unless stronger Feishu tenant evidence proves it is safe and necessary for affected deployments.

recommendation.title: Require Live Proof Then Pick Mode
recommendation.body: Collect redacted Feishu timing and CardKit PUT evidence, then reshape the fix around the mitigation that actually reduces the tail without losing final content.

likelyOwner.reason: The package metadata identifies this handle as the Feishu plugin owner, and the decision is specific to Feishu channel behavior.
